description: A dual-core ARM Cortex-M0+ (RP2040) board with GP0-GP28 broken out (minus GP23/GP24, used internally and not exposed as diagram pins), 3 of which (GP26-28) double as analog inputs.
how_to_use: I2C/SPI/UART peripherals can each be mapped to more than one physical GP pin by the sketch itself, so no single pin is hardware-fixed to a bus the way it is on an AVR board — treat any bus pin as ordinary GPIO unless the lesson's own code pins it down.

plain.what: A small, cheap and fast microcontroller board from Raspberry Pi — a different little computer you can program like an Arduino.
plain.how: Hold the BOOTSEL button while plugging in USB to load a program. Its pins are called GP0, GP1 … and it works at 3.3 V, not 5 V.
